item.title: Ireland West Airport to receive almost €2 million in funding
item.description: Ireland West Airport is set to receive over €1.9 million in Government funding. The funding is part of an overall package of €4 million announced today by the Minister for Transport, Darragh O’Brien. It's expected the funding will go towards vital safety and security operations at the airport. Official opened in 1986, Passenger numbers at Ireland West Airport in 2025 are expected to reach record levels of around 950,000. Advertisement

item.description: Roscommon will mark their return back to Division 1 football with a trip to the home of the All Ireland champions Kerry on January 25th. item.description: Local Fianna Fáil members have expressed their frustration as a review into the party's botched presidential campaign has been delayed further. Jim Gavin's legal team has requested a copy of the review before it's published. The Taoiseach informed his Fianna Fáil parliamentary party of the delay last night. item.title: Multimillion-euro Connolly Barracks hub a big boost for community groups
item.description: The cathaoirleach of Longford Municipal District says the overhaul of Connolly Barracks will be a huge boost to community groups. The historic building shut down in 2009 and is being converted into a cultural and community hub. The project has secured €7 million in funding, and it will be complete in two years’ time. item.title: Free Christmas dinner and music in Boyle on December 28th
item.description: A free Christmas dinner event is taking place in Boyle on December 28th. It’s on in Dorothy Shannon’s King House Tea Rooms, for the eighth time. To book your place, drop into the coffee shop or call 087-6430326. Advertisement Dorothy says the event gets busier every year and Christmas is a lonely time for many people.

item.title: Calls for greater investment in south Leitrim water infrastructure
item.description: The Dáil has heard the need for greater water infrastructure in south Leitrim. Significant outages have impacted many areas including Cloone, Carrigallen and Aughnasheelin. It's felt this is due to the plant being over capacity. Local TD Martin Kenny says it's a part of a wider problem nationally in terms of waste water. item.title: Elphin Credit Union to close following structural damage
item.description: Roscommon Credit Union Ltd has announced the closure of its Elphin branch after significant structural damage to the building rendered continued operations unsustainable. The decision was communicated to members in a letter issued on Wednesday, outlining the circumstances and detailing the supports that will remain available.
